clue.text: Where you might seek views of surgeons and nurses?

definitions.text: Where you might seek views of surgeons and nurses?

parts.words: Where you might seek views of surgeons and nurses?
parts.note: surgeons and nurses read as hospital staff, but surgeonfish and nurse sharks are sea creatures put on display in tanks

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where to go to watch the medical staff at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The surgeonfish and the nurse shark are both marine animals, so the place to view them is a public fish tank, not a hospital gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A public building of fish tanks is where visitors go to look at marine creatures such as these.

clue.text: A pound of tobacco

definitions.meaning: a lump of chewing tobacco held in the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for a pound coin and also names a wad of tobacco for chewing.

clue.text: Sam rebels when made to recompile computer program

indicators.note: to recompile is to put together again, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A programmer named Sam grumbles when forced to rebuild some software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made to recompile' rearranges SAM REBELS; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a program that translates assembly language into machine code, an example of computer software.

clue.text: It never really upsets solvers, having to take first letters for a quick entry

indicators.note: openly tells the solver to use only the initial letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A setter claims the clue never troubles solvers, since they just take initials.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is candid: 'to take first letters' picks the initials of the first six words; 'for' links them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden rush inwards, such as of water or air, is a fast entering.

clue.text: Mass based on C playing in cute Wigmore Hall

indicators.note: the words are put into play and rearranged, as performers at a concert venue would play

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A review of a concert in the key of C at a charming London recital venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Wigmore Hall is a London concert venue, and C looks like a musical key, but it is carbon: relative masses of molecules are measured against carbon-12. 'playing' rearranges CUTE WIGMORE HALL; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This chemistry quantity is the mass of a molecule relative to one twelfth of a carbon-12 atom.

clue.text: Calm down whenever getting into lively surrounding

indicators.note: one word enters the other and sits inside its letters

parts.note: pacy means fast-moving, lively
if can mean whenever, as in 'if it rains I stay in'

explanation.surface: Advice to settle down whenever one gets into a frantic environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' signals the container; 'surrounding' says the same thing from the outer word's side, so neither is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe or quieten someone is the same as making them calm down.

clue.text: People of medium stature?

parts.note: seems to describe people of average height, but a medium is someone who claims to contact spirits, so these are people with the standing of mediums

explanation.surface: A description of people who are neither tall nor short.
explanation.definitionFit: Clairvoyants who claim contact with the dead are known as mediums, hence people of that standing.

clue.text: What's tea passed around in?

indicators.note: one piece goes round the outside of the other, enclosing it

parts.note: cha is a British slang word for tea
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about what vessel the tea is handed round in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed around' signals the container, and the whole clue doubles as a question about the crockery tea is served in, so it works as an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain cups and saucers, the fine crockery that tea is served in, are called by this name.

clue.text: The French flag, once?

parts.note: not the tricolour but the stylised lily emblem on the banner of the old French monarchy

explanation.surface: A question about what the flag of France used to be.
explanation.walkthrough: The stylised lily was the royal emblem of France before the Revolution; 'flag' also hints at the flag iris, which the emblem may depict.
explanation.definitionFit: The heraldic lily was the emblem of the French kings and appeared on their royal banner.

clue.text: Listeners 'upset with lack of energy in my singing

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the other word
upset means knocked into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
says that something is missing from the word before

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Listeners are upset because a performance lacks energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with lack of' removes the E, 'upset' rearranges what is left into INSTRELS, and 'in' places that inside the other piece. The stray apostrophe before 'upset' is an OCR artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: Minstrelsy is the art of medieval wandering musicians, so it means song or singing.

clue.text: I'm penning note for entry into account

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone writes a note that will go into a ledger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, but it means enclosing in a pen; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A single line or entry in a list of accounts is called an item.

clue.text: Rum aesthetic set out for small-scale opera

indicators.note: set out means laid out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange artistic style is used for a little opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like an anagram signal meaning odd, but it is fodder; 'set out' rearranges RUM AESTHETIC; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage works combining drama and music, often smaller than grand opera, belong to this genre.

clue.text: Supported accommodating four mostly out under canvas

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: backed means supported
IV is four in Roman numerals

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: Someone backed a group of four who were mostly out camping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supported' looks like the definition, but 'under canvas', meaning in tents, defines the answer; 'mostly' and 'accommodating' do the cutting and enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: To camp without proper shelter, as soldiers do in tents, is to be living in temporary quarters outdoors.

clue.text: Beak's to make an announcement

definitions.meaning: to advertise or announce by posters

explanation.surface: A bird is about to announce something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' is also British slang for a magistrate, which the surface tempts, but here it is a bird's mouthpart; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's horny mouthpart has this name, and to publicise by poster is also this verb.

clue.text: Holds to fondle back, moving close together

parts.note: locks means holds fast

indicators.note: back signals that the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to pet is to fondle

explanation.surface: Someone holds another in order to caress their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a body part to be stroked, but it reverses PET to TEP; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching in step so close that each person follows the one in front exactly describes this formation.

clue.text: Fat? One ought to go on the wagon, just in case

definitions.meaning: a roll of flab round the waist

definitions.text: One ought to go on the wagon, just in case
definitions.meaning: a reserve wheel carried on a vehicle for emergencies

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the wagon' suggests giving up drink, which suits a dieter, but here it is a wheel kept on a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a bulge of fat at the waist, it is also the extra wheel carried for a puncture.

clue.text: Chose bad moment, finding fog over island and sea

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits on top of the rest

parts.note: mist is a light fog
Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Someone timed a voyage badly and met fog over an island and the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finding' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something at the wrong time is to have judged the moment badly.

clue.text: One who's upper-class in company before queen, given rank?

indicators.note: before places the preceding pieces ahead of the next

parts.note: U is the conventional label for upper-class usage
R is from Regina, Latin for queen
a tier is a rank or row

explanation.surface: A question about someone posh who mixes in society ahead of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is the definition, picked out by the whole clue's picture of an attendant at court; 'who's', 'in' and 'given' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant at a royal court is a person, someone who waits on the monarch.

clue.text: Radical involved in revolutionary liberation

indicators.note: the answer is wrapped up inside the run of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone radical is caught up in a revolutionary struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' reads as an extremist, but in chemistry a radical is a group of atoms.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry an aryl group is a radical derived from an aromatic ring compound.

clue.text: Starting on Eiger, one testing mountaineering ladder

indicators.note: only the starting letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: someone who puts things to the test, a person making an attempt

explanation.surface: A climber begins work on the Eiger, trying out equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eiger is a famous Swiss mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A short rope ladder used by climbers on steep rock is called by this French word.

clue.text: Destructive insect living in stately piles?

definitions.text: Destructive insect living in stately piles?

parts.words: Destructive insect living in stately piles?
parts.note: stately piles read as grand country houses, but piles are also the tufts of a rug, which this pest eats

explanation.surface: A pest infesting grand country homes.
explanation.definitionFit: This beetle's larvae eat woollen rugs, so it lives in the pile of floor coverings.

clue.text: Bird seed's the thing

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed
it means the thing, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: Birdseed is just what is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seed's' gives PIP with 's as a link word for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipit is a small brown songbird, a kind of bird.

clue.text: Eager to have new rising joint

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising moves the letter upward, towards the top

parts.note: keen means eager

explanation.surface: Someone keen to have a new joint fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' lifts the N of KEEN up two places, giving K, N, E, E.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the joint between the thigh and the lower leg.

clue.text: Pass over bowls captain

definitions.meaning: the captain of a team in lawn bowls

explanation.walkthrough: Lawn bowls is a British outdoor game; the captain of a team, or rink, is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to jump it, and this is also the title of a bowls team leader.

clue.text: Extolling once, making head appear big?

definitions.meaning: an old sense meaning praising or glorifying
enlarging an image, as a lens does

explanation.walkthrough: The old sense survives in 'My soul doth magnify the Lord'.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaically this verb meant glorifying, and it now means enlarging how something looks.

clue.text: Hendrix they'd regularly altered for publication

indicators.note: take every other letter, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Jimi Hendrix lyrics are routinely changed before release.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimi Hendrix was a rock guitarist.
explanation.definitionFit: Text corrected and prepared before printing has been revised for release.

clue.text: Novelist beginning to get involved in strange venture

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up within, so the letter goes inside
strange signals the letters are rearranged into an odd order
only the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A novelist starts to get involved in an odd enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges VENTURE to TURENEV, and 'involved in' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a nineteenth-century Russian writer of novels such as Fathers and Sons.
